104,532 km2 for 1010-1014. The infobox gives no area, so there is no area check. The page does not date the extent; the ledger's 1009 event carries it from the start.

101,658 km2, 1028-1033: the outline gains detail (81 vertices) where Cliopatria's Seville begins in 1028. The Seville page dates Abu al-Qasim's independence 'after its downfall in 1031' (infobox 1023) and conquests of Mértola, Niebla, Saltés, Huelva, Silves and Santa María de Algarve only 'during his reign' of Abbad II (1042-1069), so no page here dates the Seville-Badajoz frontier. 106,877 km2, 1034-1039, the largest shape (+5,200 km2 on 1028). The Aftasid page says Abdallah ibn al-Aftas (reigned 1022-1045) 'ruled over an extensive part of the Al Garb Al Andalus' reaching 'from the Douro river to south of the Tagus', which fits a shape whose northern edge is at 40.9 N. The year 1034 of the growth is Cliopatria's; no page dates it.

95,654 km2 as drawn by Cliopatria, 1056-1065: south edge raised to 37.8 N after Cliopatria's Santa Maria do Algarve, Saltés and Huelva and Niebla rows end in 1055 (absorbed by Seville: Seville page 'conquering Mertola, Niebla, Saltés and Huelva, Silves, Santa María de Algarve during his reign'). The north of Cliopatria's shape is still as large as in 1055 (bbox to 40.94 N), so it does not show the 1055 loss of the ledger. Fix pass 2026-10-25 (reviewer's blocking finding): the shape is now the part of the 1056 outline that is also in the 1066 outline (the land south of about 40 N), plus a 40 km district round Coimbra, which the taifa keeps until July 1064 (ledger: loss of Coimbra, Siege of Coimbra page). keyframe_review.note: 65,261 km2, 1066-1071, 30,400 km2 smaller than 1056: the north above 40.0 N (the Mondego and Coimbra) is lost. The page dates the tribute and loss to 1055 and the Siege of Coimbra to 1064 (Ferdinand I entered the city on 9 July 1064; the infobox lists the Taifa of Badajoz as a belligerent), so Cliopatria draws the loss two to eleven years late. The geometry is kept; the ledger moves the loss to 1055 and Coimbra to 1064. Fix pass 2026-10-25: the 1056 keyframe now carries the 1066 outline plus the Coimbra district, and the 1055 loss region no longer contains Coimbra, so the strip is lost once (1055) and Coimbra once (1064).

The page ends the second taifa in 1150 ('when it fell again under Almohad dominion'; infobox 'Conquered by the Almohads: 1150'), not 1151, and says it was 'recreated in Badajoz', whose city lies outside Cliopatria's shape. The Taifa page gives Badajoz as '1145-1150' passing to the Almohads. No area on the page.

region.text: most of ancient Lusitania, including Mérida and Lisbon

ledger.note: 1009: Sabur al-Saqlabi founds the taifa of Badajoz as the Caliphate of Córdoba falls. 'It was created by Sabur al-Saqlabi, a former slave of perhaps Slavic or Persian origin' (rulers table: Sabur 1009-1022; infobox 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1009'). The extent is the page's 'The taifa's control extended over most of ancient Lusitania, including Mérida and Lisbon', undated, read onto Cliopatria's 1010 shape.
1022: the Aftasid dynasty replaces Sabur's. 'Sabur was succeeded in 1022 by his vizier, Abdallah ibn al-Aftas, who founded the Aftasid dynasty.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Lisbon, where Sabur's sons created the short-lived taifa of Lisbon

ledger.note: 1022: Sabur's sons hold Lisbon for a moment. 'Sabur's sons fled to Lisbon, where they created the short-lived taifa of Lisbon, which was soon reconquered by Badajoz.' The rulers table gives 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sabur, 1022 (in Lisbon)'; the radius is the researcher's reading of 'Lisbon'.
Lisbon retaken. The page says only 'soon' and gives no year; placed in 1022 as a bridge (page silent). Cliopatria draws Lisbon inside the taifa throughout.

region.text: 'significant parts of its territory south of the Mondego River (south of Coimbra)', the page's words; the land is the part of Cliopatria's 1055 shape that is gone by 1066, less the district of Coimbra, which is lost separately in July 1064

ledger.note: 1055: Badajoz becomes a tributary of León-Castile and loses land. 'In 1055 Badajoz became a tributary of the Kingdom of León-Castile, losing significant parts of its territory south of the Mondego River (south of Coimbra).' The page's direction is odd for a northern power, so the region is read from Cliopatria's later shape (the Beira north of about 40 N). The tributary tint (rule 4) belongs to kingdom-of-leon's vassal_start for taifa-of-badajoz, 1055; the Aftasid page also says Badajoz 'came under the suzerainty of the Kingdom of León- Castile' in 1055. Fix pass 2026-10-25: the Coimbra district (40 km) is taken out of this region so that Coimbra is not lost twice (it is lost in July 1064, below); about 28,600 km2 remain (gazetteer), the Beira north of about 40 N. The Ferdinand I of León page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Le%C3%B3n) dates conquests inside or beside this strip later than the tribute: 'On 29 November 1057 his army conquered Lamego and its valleys' and Viseu 'on 25 July 1058' (Coimbra 'on 25 July 1064' there, against 9 July on the Siege page); it says only that 'it is possible that as early as 1055 Ferdinand attacked the taifa of Badajoz'. The year 1055 is the Taifa of Badajoz page's and is kept at confidence 2; the strip may have been lost piecemeal in 1055-1058. These conquests, all on or north of the Mondego, support reading the page's 'south of the Mondego' as the land north of the Mondego-Coimbra line.

region.text: the city of Coimbra and its district

ledger.note: 1064 (January): Ferdinand I besieges Coimbra. 'They arrived before the walls of the city on 20 January 1064.' The page does not name the taifa holding the city; its infobox lists the Taifa of Badajoz among the belligerents.

region.text: the city of Coimbra and its district

ledger.note: 1064 (July): Coimbra falls after a siege of about six months. 'King Ferdinand entered the city on 9 July 1064' (a stray line gives 25 July).

region.text: the city of Coimbra and its district

ledger.note: 1064: Coimbra passes to León. 'The city was then delivered to Sesnando Davides, who ruled it as Count of Coimbra until his death in 1091.' About 5,000 Muslims were taken captive. Cliopatria's 1066 shape (30,000 km2 smaller) is the drawing of this and the 1055 loss.

1094: the Almoravids occupy Badajoz. 'In 1094 the Almoravids occupied Badajoz and Yahya was killed together with two of his sons.' The Almoravid page: 'the Almoravids seized control of the entire Taifa kingdom of Badajoz' after its ruler sought an alliance with Castile; the Aftasid page adds that the city 'was taken at the end of 1095'. The state is absent from the map 1095-1143.

region.text: Badajoz and its district, where 'a second independent taifa was briefly recreated'

ledger.note: 1144: Badajoz is independent again. 'a second independent taifa was briefly recreated in Badajoz, existing from 1144 to 1150'. The Almoravid page dates the start of the collapse to 'A Muridun revolt broke out in southwestern Iberia in 1144'. The page gives no extent; the region is Cliopatria's 1147 shape plus the city.

1150: the Almohads take Badajoz. 'a second independent taifa was briefly recreated in Badajoz, existing from 1144 to 1150, when it fell again under Almohad dominion'; infobox 'Conquered by the Almohads: 1150'. The Taifa page gives 'Badajoz 1145-1150 passed to the Almohads'. Cliopatria carries the shape to 1151.

1150: the taifa of Badajoz ends under the Almohads (see the loss event); the page's later sentence says its original territory was 'controlled by various kingdoms (Almoravids, Almohads, Portugal) in succession'.

wars.name: Siege of Coimbra (1064)

zones.text: the city of Coimbra and its district

wars.outcome: Ferdinand I of León took Coimbra on 9 July 1064 after a siege begun on 20 January; Sesnando Davides became Count of Coimbra.
wars.note: The page's body never names the taifa holding Coimbra; the infobox lists Badajoz as a belligerent.

wars.name: Battle of Sagrajas
wars.outcome: On 23 October 1086 Alfonso VI was defeated near Badajoz; no frontier moved, but Yahya of Badajoz, fearing Almoravid power, then allied with Alfonso.
wars.note: Badajoz page: 'His troops fought alongside the Almoravid dynasty against the Christian army in the Battle of Sagrajas (1086), which occurred not far from Badajoz.'

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the Taifa of Badajoz
wars.outcome: The Almoravids occupied Badajoz in 1094 and annexed the taifa; the Aftasid ruler Yahya (or al-Mutawakkil) was killed with two sons.
wars.note: The Almoravid page: 'the Almoravids seized control of the entire Taifa kingdom of Badajoz'; it gives no date for the ruler's death. The Aftasid page has the city fall at the end of 1095.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the second Taifa of Badajoz
wars.outcome: The second taifa (1144-1150) fell to the Almohads in 1150; Portugal later controlled part of the original territory.
wars.note: No battle or campaign is named on the page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any page opened. The Douro-Tagus reach, the Mondego line (1055) and the Coimbra frontier (1064) are described in words only; Cliopatria's western taifa borders are approximate throughout.

notes: Taifa of Badajoz, 1009-1094 and 1144-1150 in one dossier (Cliopatria rows 1010-1093 and 1147-1151, one Cliopatria Name). Page budget 5, six pages opened (the Almoravid page is shared with the other taifas). UNSETTLED: (1) the page's 1055 sentence puts the lost land 'south of the Mondego River (south of Coimbra)', which is probably a garbled description of the land north of the Mondego; the 1055 loss region is read from Cliopatria's 1066 shape and is confidence 2. (2) The rulers table is internally inconsistent (Yahya 1067-1073/1079 in the table, yet the text has him at Sagrajas in 1086 and killed in 1094; Siddray ibn Wazir listed 1142-1145 beside a taifa dated 1144-1150), so identity.rulers is omitted. (3) The Abbadid (Seville) conquests of Badajoz territory are undated on every page opened; Cliopatria's 1028, 1034, 1040 and 1056 changes are therefore unexplained by events and the verdicts say so. (4) The Almoravid takeover is 1094 on the Badajoz, Almoravid and Aftasid pages, but the Aftasid page also says the city was taken at the end of 1095. (5) Cliopatria's 1147-1151 shape sits around Évora-Elvas and misses the city of Badajoz; the correction adds the city. (6) Kingdom-of-leon should carry a vassal_start for taifa-of-badajoz in 1055 (tributary, rule 4) and the Coimbra gain in 1064; kingdom-of-castile also borders Badajoz in Cliopatria 1046-1065 and the page says 'León-Castile'. (7) Counterpart 'Taifa of Lisbon (Banu Sabur)' (1022) has no Cliopatria row and needs a short dossier or a note in the Portugal batch. Region names used that the gazetteer may lack: none beyond places already in it. FIX PASS 2026-10-25 (author, after the reviewer's FAIL): (a) Keyframe taifa-of-badajoz_1056 is now 'adjust' with the reviewer's whole corrected shape (the 1056 outline within the 1066 outline, plus a 40 km district round Coimbra, until 1064); the 1055 loss region is now the 1055 shape minus the 1066 shape minus the Coimbra district, so Coimbra is lost once, in July 1064. Both resolve in the gazetteer (248 and 113 cells). (b) The Ferdinand I of León page dates Lamego (29 Nov 1057) and Viseu (25 July 1058) and has Coimbra on 25 July 1064 (the Siege page: 9 July); it does not date the 1055 tribute or any loss of Badajoz land. I keep 1055 (the Taifa of Badajoz page, confidence 2) but the strip north of 40 N may have gone in 1055-1058, and the page's 'south of the Mondego' is still read as 'north' (unsettled). (c) Thin items: the Aftasid dynasty page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aftasid_dynasty) does not mention Lisbon or Sabur's sons, so the Lisbon reconquest ('soon') stays a confidence-1 bridge in 1022; the Ferdinand I page has no Abbadid conquest of Badajoz land (only a ransom paid by Seville, 'and probably Badajoz also', in 1063), so Cliopatria's changes of 1018, 1028, 1034, 1040 and 1056 stay without events. The page budget (5) is now exceeded by three pages (Ferdinand I, Aftasid, Taifa of Badajoz re-read), all named by the reviewer.
